public_source.title: The Nordstrom-Robinson Code is the Binary Image of the Octacode
public_source.formula_evidence: The paper identifies the Nordstrom-Robinson code as the octacode's Gray image and gives its minimum distance as 6.
public_source.parameter_transfer: Append one zero coordinate to the (16,256,6) Nordstrom-Robinson code; this preserves every pairwise distance and gives a (17,256,6) code.

verification.source_review: Reviewed the full public Forney-Sloane-Trott octacode paper and the Magma manual generator matrix and Gray map. Exact replay and independent all-pairs check give 256 words and distance6 after zero extension. Milshtein reported258 stays separate; no 258-word witness is claimed.

source.paper_title: A new two-error-correcting binary code of length 16
source.author: Moshe Milshtein
source.evidence: Brouwer attributes A(17,6) >= 258 to Milshtein. His paper abstract reports a (16,258,5) construction; appending an overall parity bit gives a (17,258,6) construction.

access_checks.result: Only the abstract and first-page preview were exposed; the codeword table was unavailable.

access_checks.source: Springer Nature article page and public search
access_checks.result: The public page exposes the abstract and references. The /tables/1 and /fulltext.html endpoints were not publicly readable in this check. Searches found no author manuscript, repository copy, or supplementary codeword file. Full-text API access requires a relevant license or agreement and was not used.

The work entry links only to the DOI, and the public profile has no researcher website URL.

limitations: No 258-word codeword list has been obtained or independently verified, so the 258 lower bound is recorded as reported rather than reproduced.
The reproduced 256-word witness is below the highest reported value of 258; it is not marked as matching the best public result.
Milshtein's 258-word witness remains unavailable in the public sources checked, so the benchmark has no verified 258-word artifact yet.

best_human.provenance: Brouwer's table attributes A(17,6) >= 258 to Moshe Milshtein. The construction is an overall-parity extension of his length-16, distance-5 code.
best_human.evidence_state: published_lower_bound; word list unavailable and not independently reproduced

best_public.evidence_state: public lower bound; not an independently verified witness; table gives upper bound 340
best_public.origin_type: unknown unless attribution is stated in source/provenance

best_reproduced.provenance: Primitive binary BCH [15,7,5] code generated by x^8+x^7+x^6+x^4+1, extended by an overall parity bit and one zero coordinate.
best_reproduced.ai_provenance: Witness generated from the stated polynomial and all 128 messages; all pairs were checked by the task validator.
best_reproduced.evidence_state: witness and pairwise minimum distance independently checked exactly

survey_scope_note: Best public means the strongest same-parameter result in the cited checked sources. This is not a claim that every public source has been surveyed. Unmatched parameters are listed separately.
frozen_human_baseline_type: reconstruction of a published human method; weaker than best public record
